sourceInformation.source: Densha de Go! (the train-driving simulation series): a notched master controller, stopping on a marker, a timetable kept to the second, ATS, point-and-call calls.
sourceInformation.perspective: First-person cab in pseudo-3D, with chase and front cameras and a side-view Stop Cam replay after every stop
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge v0.85.2 (2D engine: game loop, input, menus, Shell pause/settings/controls, Dialog, Humanoid, chip audio, headless advance), plain JavaScript, a custom pseudo-3D rail renderer (src/30-render.js), AI Hub client session.js 1.4.0. Tests: Node 24 and Playwright 1.63 (Chromium).
sourceInformation.artDirection: The engine's native look: 427x240 low-resolution pixels, hue-shifted shading and the pixel font, with a hand-built segment-based pseudo-3D world (stations, strips, buildings, trains, catenary, fog, night lights).
sourceInformation.animation: The engine's Humanoid rig for the talking portraits, plus code-driven animation: the lever handle and needle, the pointing glove, wipers, rain, crowd sway, crossing gates, the Stop Cam replay.
sourceInformation.audio: All code: the engine chip synth for effects and songs, plus a Web Audio train soundscape (rumble, rails, wind, motor, brake squeal, horn, rain), station departure melodies and Animalese-style gibberish voices for every character.
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1, ghost mode: the Parallel Run for 1 to 4 players, with the other players shown as coloured ghost trains. Passes the hub harness.
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Node tests (124 checks: physics, ATS, signals, stops, the whole career played by the autopilot through the real scenes, attract mode, dev mode), a Playwright browser smoke test, and the AI Hub harness (1, 2 and 4 players, latency and loss, host leaves).
sourceInformation.research: Read the engine card (README, API.md, the road kit) and the AI Hub README, and followed PLAN.md. No web research; the source is described from general knowledge.
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux (WSL2); browser tests in headless Chromium, player browser unknown

testingFeedback: How many issues did testing catch? About 9 real game issues.

How many were critical? 3: the train could freeze at a hair above 0 km/h and never be judged, a stop more than 80 m past the marker was never judged, and a finished shift left a flag set that hung the next one.
Most helpful test: the scripted career, where the autopilot drives all six stages through the real title, map, briefing, drive and results scenes.
Least helpful: screenshots from software-rendered headless Chromium for anything that depends on timing; they only show a frame.
engineFeedback: What did you like most? Exact fixed steps with game.advance, so the whole game plays headless and deterministically, plus the free pause, settings and controls screens.
Did you get stuck or guess wrong? Input.tap() marks the device as touch, which tripped my touch-only gate in tests; and the pause-menu items need game.resume() themselves.
Most important thing to build yourself: the rail renderer (segments, platforms, strips, trains, catenary, fog, night) and the train physics, ATS and timetable.
Hardest part: the engine had no multi-track or rear-camera road module, so everything projected had to be written from scratch on top of the pixel primitives.

What did you change? Dialog voice can be a function (for gibberish speech); the glyph default is PlayStation; ChipAudio.bus() and noiseBuffer() for the game's own sound; and Options is ignored while Create is held in a hub session. See ENGINE-CHANGES.md.
One thing to change: a first-class pseudo-3D road/rail module with multiple tracks, long side objects and rear cameras.
promptFeedback: What did you like most? A concrete plan with a clear core loop, and hard rules (no stubs, tests behind one command, the hub harness as a gate).
What was confusing? PLAN.md is very large and prescribes more than the TASK needs (a local duel, engine forks, rig poses), so triage was needed; and the title RNG step was already done by the plan.
Hardest thing: breadth. Menus, dev mode, attract mode, story, voices, hub and a new renderer all have to be finished in one session.
What would you change? Split the plan into must, should and could, and say which engine patches are optional.

aiHub.name: Densha de Halo!
aiHub.tagline: Hello by train. Stop on the mark.
aiHub.description: Drive the Halo Line ring railway: notch the lever, obey signals and ATS, point and call, and stop on the marker on the second. A short story, six shifts and an online Parallel Run.
aiHub.controls: Lever R2/L2 or W/S, neutral R1/N, emergency brake L1/Backspace, point and call Cross/E, horn Square/Space, ATS confirm Triangle/Q, view Circle/C. Mouse: wheel and cab buttons.
